title: The Illusion of Progress: Re-evaluating Hallucination Detection in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the correlation between generated response lengths and hallucination detection metric scores (e.g., ROUGE), and conducting controlled experiments with systematic text repetition to demonstrate that metrics systematically penalize or reward responses based on verbosity regardless of factual accuracy.

Conducting qualitative and quantitative error analysis comparing ROUGE scores against human judgments and LLM-as-Judge semantic evaluations to show a systemic metric preference for structurally similar but factually incorrect answers over semantically equivalent but lexically distinct ones.
